newsitem.title: CHINA: Engelhard plans $50-$100 mln China venture.
newsitem.headline: Engelhard plans $50-$100 mln China venture.

text.p: U.S.-based Engelhard Corp is planning a $50-$100 million catalyst joint venture with China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec), the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The new venture would have production capacity of 40,000 to 50,000 tonnes of fluid cracking catalysts (FCCs) a year and would market its goods in China and abroad, the newspaper said.
"Engelhard sees great market potential in China and the fast-growing Asia-Pacific region," the newspaper quoted Engelhard Asia Pacific president George Hsu as saying.
Engelhard forecast China's consumption of FCCs would grow to 80,000 tonnes a year by 2000 from the current 60,000 tonnes a year, Hsu said.
Demand in other Asia-Pacific countries would rise by 50 percent over the next several years, Hsu said.
The new plant would be set up with the Changling Petroleum Process and Chemical Complex, a Sinopec subsidiary in Changsha, capital of central Hunan province, the newspaper said.
Engelhard would complete a feasibility study by next July and was aiming to start production by 1999, Hsu said.
The venture would be Engelhard's first in China, although the company had already opened representative offices in Beijing and Shanghai, the newspaper said.
The firm was looking into setting up a possible venture to produce kaolin, a major raw material used in the manufacture of FCCs, Hsu said.
Fluid cracking catalysts are used by petroleum refiners to break down crude oil into petrol and other products.
